laws.rule: Under the Telangana Prohibition Act, 1995, selling, buying, possessing or consuming liquor otherwise than in accordance with that Act or the Telangana Excise Act, 1968 is prohibited. Production, manufacture, storage, possession, collection, purchase, sale and transport of arrack are prohibited.

Being found in a state of intoxication in a public place, otherwise than as permitted under any law, is an offence under the Prohibition Act: imprisonment of at least two months and up to one year, or a fine of up to two thousand rupees, or both. For this section, intoxication means a state of mind and behaviour in which a person is incapable of knowing the nature of their actions or of judging the consequences, by reason of intoxication.

local-law.note: Official Act text was read from the India Code text extract for this item. This is not a total ban on liquor: the Prohibition Act requires liquor other than arrack to be held and consumed in accordance with the Telangana Excise Act, 1968. Federal narcotics rules belong on India's page.

items.text: Telangana is not a dry state for all liquor, but arrack is prohibited, and other liquor may be sold, possessed or consumed only in accordance with the Telangana Prohibition Act, 1995 and the Telangana Excise Act, 1968. Being found intoxicated in a public place, otherwise than as permitted under any law, is an offence.
